references.text: The first census in the wilderness counted 603,550 men, which can be compared to the result of this second count at 601,730 men.
Summary of the first census, which also gave a total of 603,550 fighting men from Israel.
At the time of leaving Egypt, there were about 600,000 men on foot, showing that the size of the people remained relatively stable throughout the wilderness journey.
The census connected with the building of the tabernacle showed 603,550 men, confirming the number of the people.
This census was carried out by Moses and Eleazar, and no one from the first census remained except Caleb and Joshua.
